title: agentic-foundation repository configuration (v2)
description: Schema for .agentic/config.yml — a platform-neutral contract for a graph of agent stages. It lists exactly the keys the neutral pipeline reads; a key that is not listed here does nothing. Keys that are not part of the contract at the top level (for example operator tooling such as `deploy:`) are ignored, never rejected. Inside a Stagr key (`platform`, `defaults`, `stages`, ...) an unknown key is an error. Secrets are referenced by NAME only; values never live here. See docs/CONFIGURATION.md.

profile.description: Onboarding shortcut. Expands to a default stage graph that `stages` can then override by id. `custom` adds no stages (you define them all).

platform.description: The SCM/CI platform this repo lives on. The contract is platform-neutral; a per-platform renderer maps it to that system's pipeline. Which renderers exist today is in docs/ARCHITECTURE.md, section 8.

trusted_roles.description: Normalized author-permission levels allowed to drive agentic changes; the renderer maps them to the platform's own roles.

publisher.description: OPTIONAL. The Stagr GitHub App that publishes Stagr-owned platform signals (Check Runs). The operator creates the App and stores its private key as a repository secret, named in `secrets.app_private_key`.

app_id.description: Numeric ID of the Stagr GitHub App (a positive integer, or a string of digits with no leading zero). Not a secret: it is rendered as a literal into generated workflows. No default; required whenever the neutral pipeline needs the publisher.

app_slug.description: The App's slug: the lowercase name in its URL, github.com/apps/<slug>. When it is required: docs/CONFIGURATION.md, `publisher.app_slug`.

defaults.description: Fallbacks for stages that do not set their own provider or model. A stage left with no provider after these fallbacks fails validation; a stage with no model binds none and the backend chooses (see docs/CONFIGURATION.md, Model resolution).

provider.description: Default provider id for stages that omit one. The only provider with a default backend today is `openai` (Codex).

models.description: Default model binding per provider id (open map — any provider).

secrets.description: OPTIONAL. The NAME of the repository secret holding each credential Stagr uses, never a value. Every entry has a default; set one only when your secret is named differently. When each one is needed: docs/CONFIGURATION.md, section 2.

app_private_key.description: The Stagr GitHub App's private key. Default: STAGR_APP_PRIVATE_KEY.

platform_token.description: A real user's token, used to post review requests and resolve review threads. Default: REMEDIATION_TOKEN.

openai_api_key.description: The OpenAI API key of the `codex-api` backend. Default: OPENAI_API_KEY.

anthropic_api_key.description: The Anthropic API key of the `remediation` agent. Default: ANTHROPIC_API_KEY.

stages.description: The agent pipeline as an ordered, extensible graph. Merged onto the `profile`'s stages (a stage here with the same id overrides the profile's).

enabled.description: Set false to disable the fast-path lane so every PR (docs included) is routed to every stage.

remediation.description: OPTIONAL. Automated fixes for review findings: an agent reads each review from the stages' review backends and from trusted human reviewers, fixes the findings it judges real, and declines the rest with its reasons. Omit to fix findings by hand.

provider.description: The agent that fixes findings. anthropic: Claude Code Action, through the Claude GitHub App.

max_rounds.description: Automated fix rounds per pull request. When reached with findings still open, the pull request is handed to a human. Default: 5.

discussions.description: Discussion-resolution requirement for the merge gate.

require_resolved.description: When true, all open review discussions must be resolved before the merge gate passes. Default: false (discussion state is not checked).

stage.description: One stage in the pipeline. `id` and `type` are required. Provider and model resolve from the stage, then `defaults`; the backend is the provider's default unless the stage pins one.

id.description: Unique stage id, e.g. review, security.

type.description: What kind of work the stage does. Mirrors the StageKind enum of the neutral core.

provider.description: Provider id for this stage. Omit to inherit defaults.provider.

backend.description: Backend that performs the stage. Omit to use the provider's default backend (`openai` -> `codex`). `openai` also offers `codex-api`: Codex run in the pipeline on an OpenAI API key.

skill.description: Skill id: the stage's methodology. Resolves to the repository's .agentic/skills/<id>/SKILL.md when present, otherwise to the shipped stagr/templates/skills/<id>/SKILL.md.

gate.description: advisory = reported, never blocks merge; blocking = the merge gate requires the stage to pass. Omit for advisory.

depends_on.description: Ids of stages that must reach conclusion=PASS before this one starts (defines the graph).

modelBinding.description: Model binding: the literal model id to use.

secretName.description: The NAME of a CI secret: letters, digits and underscores, not starting with a digit, without the GITHUB_ prefix that GitHub reserves. Names are placed into generated workflows as `secrets.<name>`, so anything else is rejected instead of rendered.
